currentContext.strengths: Extensive omni-channel distribution network of 130 fulfilment centres and 95 branded retail stores across South, West and Central India|Long-standing partnerships with leading national brands across steel (JSW, SAIL, AM/NS India, APL Apollo) and non-steel categories (Jaquar, Kohler, Kajaria, Nippon Paint, Polycab, Havells)|Established omni-channel presence combining physical stores/warehousing with own e-commerce platform (Buildpro Store) and marketplace listings (Amazon, Flipkart)|Over five decades of industry experience and an established, diversified customer base across retail, contractor and institutional segments|Deep market penetration strategy targeting smaller cities and emerging towns rather than only metros, supporting a resilient, geographically diversified revenue base
currentContext.strategies: Deep market penetration and localized customer engagement, with expansion efforts focused on smaller cities and emerging towns rather than only metropolitan markets|Build a large, diversified customer base across multiple geographies and customer profiles to create a resilient, scalable business model that can sustain demand across economic cycles|Continue strengthening the omni-channel building materials platform spanning retail stores, distribution/channel and enterprise sales, and e-commerce (Buildpro Store plus Amazon and Flipkart)|Leverage the FY26 demerger and independent listing to pursue sharper business focus, improved capital allocation and greater operational flexibility as a standalone retail/distribution entity distinct from the parent's manufacturing operations|Extend geographic footprint from its core South India base (Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Goa, Puducherry) into Western and Central India (Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Odisha)|The Board's Dividend Distribution Policy sets out the external and internal factors and financial parameters considered in determining dividend distribution and how retained earnings are utilised, including the circumstances under which shareholders may or may not expect a dividend. During FY26 the policy was amended to explicitly provide for declaration of dividend in years of exceptional gains or other events. For FY26 the Board recommended a final dividend of Rs.5/- per equity share, to be formally declared at the ensuing (3rd) AGM.
currentContext.expansion: FY26 was dominated by the demerger of the omni-channel trading business from Shankara Building Products Limited into Shankara Buildpro Limited (NCLT Bengaluru Bench, appointed date April 1, 2024) and the Company's subsequent independent stock-exchange listing, creating a focused retail and distribution platform distinct from the parent's manufacturing/processing operations. Growth during the year came from continued geographic expansion of the omni-channel footprint into smaller cities and emerging towns and into Western and Central India (Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Odisha), alongside build-out of the e-commerce channel (Buildpro Store plus Amazon and Flipkart), rather than from a named plant/capacity project — the business is an asset-light retail, distribution and e-commerce network (130 fulfilment centres including 95 stores) rather than a manufacturer.
currentContext.mdna: Sustained government capital expenditure, infrastructure expansion and urbanization continuing to support structural growth in building materials demand|Government infrastructure programmes (PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, National Infrastructure Pipeline, Smart Cities Mission, PM Awas Yojana, Jal Jeevan Mission) expected to generate sustained multi-year demand across steel, pipes, roofing and allied construction materials|Steel demand growing at an estimated 8-10% year-on-year|Retail building materials growth supported by rising home construction/renovation activity, growth in Tier-2/Tier-3 cities, increasing preference for branded/quality-assured products, expansion of contractor-led and project-based purchasing, and a shift from fragmented local procurement to integrated supply solutions|Gradual, ongoing transition of the market from unorganised trade to organised retail and omni-channel distribution models, aided by growing digital adoption for product discovery and ordering|India's economy expected to grow around 6.5-7% in FY27 per RBI/global analyst projections, supporting domestic demand, though geopolitical tensions (U.S.-Iran conflict), India's high fossil-fuel import dependence, rising petroleum prices and rupee depreciation are flagged as headwinds that could stoke inflation and dampen customer sentiment|Company's high exposure to steel, a largely commoditised category, exposes it to periodic price volatility that can affect both demand patterns and margins

risks.risk: Intense market/pricing competition from organised and unorganised players
risks.note: The retail building materials industry is highly competitive and fragmented; aggressive pricing by small, owner-driven trading businesses and expanding informal trade channels (flexible credit, localised relationships) constrain the Company's pricing power and margins, particularly in commoditised categories such as steel.

risks.risk: Customer credit risk from extended trade cycles
risks.note: The business is significantly exposed to credit risk given its customer base of contractors, builders, fabricators, wholesalers and trade intermediaries, who typically transact on extended credit; delays or defaults in payment can adversely impact cash flows and the working-capital cycle.

A large, diverse SKU base spanning steel, tiles, sanitaryware, plumbing, electricals and allied products creates risk of slow-moving/obsolete stock (tiles and sanitaryware face design/model/colour obsolescence) and of breakage during storage, handling and transport of fragile products, impacting margins and working-capital efficiency.

risks.risk: High revenue concentration in commoditised steel
risks.note: Approximately 90% of Company turnover comes from the steel segment, a largely commoditised product category subject to periodic price volatility that can affect both demand patterns and margin performance.

risks.risk: Cyclicality tied to housing, real estate and infrastructure investment
risks.note: The building materials industry is cyclical and closely linked to macroeconomic conditions, particularly housing demand and infrastructure investment cycles; interest-rate changes, inflationary pressures and delays in infrastructure execution can adversely affect demand in the short term.

India imports around 80% of its fossil energy needs (about 40% from the Middle East); the prolonged U.S.-Iran conflict, resulting energy-supply disruption, sharply higher petroleum prices and rupee depreciation could stoke inflation and dampen customer sentiment, indirectly affecting demand.

one-line thesis: Shankara Buildpro delivered a strong first full-year post-demerger with 30% revenue growth and 47bps margin expansion, driven by steel volume milestones (1M tonnes) and operating leverage. The key investment narrative shifts to FY27 where management targets 20% volume growth and a 25% rebound in non-steel despite near-term demand softness and input cost volatility.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 6,826cr (+30% YoY); Q4: INR 1,996cr (+28% YoY). EBITDA: INR 228cr (+51% YoY); Margin: 3.35% (+47bps YoY); Q4 Margin: 3.51%. PAT: INR 128cr (+64% YoY); Normalized PAT excludes INR 2.61cr labor code provision. Order Book: N/A (Marketplace model). Net Debt: Not explicitly stated; Working Capital Cycle improved to 25 days; Finance cost 0.63% of revenue. One-offs: Q4 included INR 16cr exceptional costs (INR 11cr bad debt, INR 2.5cr demerger, INR 2.5cr rent) offset by INR 15cr inventory gain.
guidance: FY27 Revenue Growth: ~20%. FY27 Steel Volume: 1.2M tonnes (+~18-20%); FY28: 1.4M tonnes. FY27 Non-Steel Revenue: INR 750cr (+25%); FY28: INR 925cr. Margin Target: ~3.3-3.5% for FY27 (conservative), aspiring to 4% in 2-3 years (by FY29). Capex: INR 15-20cr for 7-10 new fulfillment centers in FY27.
order book & pipeline: Not applicable (distribution/marketplace model operates on immediate fulfillment); Steel volumes FY26: 1.016M tonnes; Q4: 2.89L tonnes.
segment / subsidiary detail: Steel: INR 6,220cr (+33% YoY), 32% volume growth; mix includes tubes (6.9L tonnes), flats, longs. Non-Steel: INR 606cr (+2% YoY), impacted by tile/plastic pipe headwinds; EBITDA margin ~6.5% vs Steel ~3%. E-commerce: INR 22cr (+322% YoY).
growth verticals / optionality: Non-steel mix shift target (15-20% of revenue in 3-5 years vs <10% currently); Geographic penetration in Tier-2/3/4; New categories (UPVC roofing, electrical, paints); Store network expansion (7-10 new centers in FY27).
margins & cost dynamics: FY26 EBITDA margin 3.35% (up 47bps); Q4 margin 3.51%. Headwinds: Natural gas prices impacting tile supply chain; PVC resin volatility. Tailwinds: Operating leverage (expenses grew 7-8% vs revenue 30%); Product mix improvement; Safeguard duties stabilizing domestic steel prices.
capex / expansion: INR 15-20cr planned for FY27 primarily for 7-10 new fulfillment centers/stores (3 already opened in Vasai, Trichur, Bangalore).
capital allocation: Organic expansion of fulfillment network; Working capital optimization (25-day cycle); No M&A mentioned; Dividend policy not discussed in transcript.
risks & watch-items: Near-term demand slowdown in Q1 FY27 due to price hikes (tiles/steel); Morbi tile cluster supply disruptions; Raw material volatility (PVC, Gas); Competition from new-age startups and large corporates in metros; Execution risk on non-steel recovery.
management quality / tone: Confident on long-term structural story and volume targets; Conservative on near-term margin guidance (3.3-3.5%) despite strong operating leverage; Acknowledges Q1 softness but expects H2 recovery.
non-obvious takeaways: Inventory gains/losses significantly impact quarterly PAT (Q4 had INR 15cr gain vs INR 8-9cr loss in prior quarters); Top 10 customers contribute only ~1% of revenue indicating extreme fragmentation; 50-50 split between retail and non-retail (OE/Dealer) in steel business.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply disruption and gas price hikes in Morbi cluster | Shankara Buildpro Limited | beneficiary | Med | As a distributor with diversified sourcing, they can navigate local manufacturing shutdowns better than pure-play manufacturers, though pricing power is temporarily constrained. |
| Volatility in steel prices impacting inventory values | Shankara Buildpro Limited | beneficiary | High | Robust inventory management and mixed customer base (retail/OE) allow them to hedge volatility better than smaller traders; recent quarter showed ability to capture inventory gains. |

themes.title: Metals & mining cycle - steel, aluminium, critical minerals
themes.need: Domestic demand growth, safeguard duties and an India capacity-expansion wave lift integrated metals while critical-mineral security gains policy support. TATASTEEL targets 45-50 MT India (FY26 India EBITDA INR34,272cr at 24% margin) with a +INR6,000/t 1QFY27 realisation uplift; JINDALSTEL/SAIL/JSWSTEEL-tier on steel; HINDALCO/NALCO on aluminium; HINDZINC on zinc (Q1FY27 all-time-record EBITDA INR8,074cr +109% YoY on a record-low zinc cost-of-production USD851/t, though CEO Arun Misra hands over to ex-SAIL chief Amarendu Prakash 1-Aug-2026 and a new Gundlupet REE/Yttrium critical-minerals block won this quarter is a 2031-32-dated option, not near-term); NMDC/COALINDIA/LLOYDSME/SARDAEN on iron-ore/coal/integrated mining. Q1FY27 also quantified the export-side shock and the downstream escape from it: JINDALSAW's consolidated PAT fell 78% YoY to INR 91cr on +9% revenue because the Strait-of-Hormuz blockade suspended ALL India-origin MENA export shipments from March 2026, holding utilisation at ~60-65%; SHYAMMETL took the other route, posting INR 5,455cr revenue (+23.3%) at a multi-quarter-high 14.9% EBITDA margin with aluminium EBITDA/t +52% YoY and specialty alloys near 20.5% margin, self-funding ~INR 9,580cr of balance capex with no debt.
themes.driver: Steel price/realisation uplift into Q1; safeguard-duty support; Hormuz reopening for line-pipe exports; value-added/downstream mix; iron-ore + critical-mineral volume ramp.

themes.title: Building-materials & home-improvement up-cycle
themes.need: The residential up-cycle pulls a broad finishing/home-improvement basket - tiles & sanitaryware (KAJARIACER/CERA/SOMANYCERA/ORIENTBELL/HINDWAREAP), wood-panels & laminates (CENTURYPLY/GREENPANEL/GREENLAM/RUSHIL/STYLAMIND), pipes/adhesives (PIDILITIND/SUPREMEIND/ASTRAL-tier) and paints (ASIANPAINT/CARYSIL/SIRCA). Premiumization + GST formalization shift share to organized players.
themes.driver: Festive/real-estate completion demand; GST 2.0 + commodity tailwinds; capacity commissioning and channel restocking.

hero.oneLiner: One of India's leading omni-channel marketplaces for building and construction products, distributing steel and allied building materials to homeowners, contractors, fabricators, institutions and industrial consumers through retail, distribution and e-commerce.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: One of India's leading omni-channel marketplaces for building and construction products, distributing steel and allied building materials to homeowners, contractors, fabricators, institutions and industrial consumers through retail, distribution and e-commerce.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Shankara Buildpro Limited is an omni-channel retailer and distributor of building and construction products, operating across steel products (pipes, TMT bars, angles/channels, heavy structurals, HR/CR/CC/GP/GC flat steel) and non-steel categories (plumbing and sanitaryware, flooring/tiles, electricals, paints, roofing, adhesives and hardware). It sources from reputed national brands (JSW Steel, SAIL, AM/NS India, APL Apollo, Jaquar, Kohler, Kajaria, Nippon Paint, Polycab, Havells, among others) and sells through 95 branded retail stores, a distribution/channel and enterprise business, and an e-commerce platform (Buildpro Store plus Amazon and Flipkart marketplaces). The Company emerged as an independent listed entity in FY26 following the demerger of the omni-channel trading business from Shankara Building Products Limited.

group_structure.title: Group structure (profile)
group_structure.body:
- Purple Splash Materials Private Limited — subsidiary: 51% held subsidiary, incorporated April 20, 2025 (CIN U24311KA2025PTC201613), registered office Bengaluru; per BRSR does not participate in the Company's Business Responsibility initiative
- Shankara Building Products Limited — related party: Was the Company's holding company until 26 September 2025; SBL was demerged from Shankara Building Products Limited's omni-channel trading business (appointed date April 1, 2024)
- Shankara Holdings Private Limited — related party: Listed as a related party in the Related Party Transactions note (enterprise in which Key Managerial Personnel/relatives have significant influence, per the note's categorisation)
- Taurus Value Steel & Pipes Private Limited — related party: Listed as a related party in the Related Party Transactions note (enterprise in which Key Managerial Personnel have significant influence)
- Vishal Precision Steel Tubes and Strips Private Limited — related party: Listed as a related party in the Related Party Transactions note (enterprise in which Key Managerial Personnel have significant influence)
- Steel Network (Holdings) Pte Limited — related party: Listed as a related party; struck off w.e.f. 26 December 2025
- Centurywells Roofing India Private Limited — related party: Listed as a related party in the Related Party Transactions note (enterprise in which Key Managerial Personnel have significant influence)
- The Café at Saanchi — related party: Enterprise in which relatives of Key Managerial Personnel have significant influence
- Shankara Buildpro Employees Gratuity Fund — related party: Entity where control exists — the Company's employee gratuity fund

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Steel: INR 6,220cr (+33% YoY), 32% volume growth; mix includes tubes (6.9L tonnes), flats, longs. Non-Steel: INR 606cr (+2% YoY), impacted by tile/plastic pipe headwinds; EBITDA margin ~6.5% vs Steel ~3%. E-commerce: INR 22cr (+322% YoY).

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Steel segment (~90% of turnover):** Steel pipes, TMT bars, Angles and channels, Heavy structurals, HR sheets/plates/coils, CR sheets and coils, Color Coated (CC) coils and profiles, GP/GC sheets and coils
- **Plumbing and sanitaryware:** CP fittings, Sanitaryware, PVC pipes and fittings
- **Flooring:** Ceramic tiles, Laminates, Fotia (private label)
- **Electricals:** Cables and fittings
- **Paints, adhesives and sealants:** Paints, Waterproofing solutions, Construction chemicals, Adhesives and sealants
- **Roofing and allied:** Steel roofing profiles, PUFF panels, UPVC sheets, Fabrication accessories

end_markets.body:
- South India (Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Goa, Puducherry)
- Western India (Maharashtra, Gujarat)
- Central India (Madhya Pradesh, Odisha)
- Individual homeowners
- Contractors, fabricators and builders
- Institutions and small-to-mid-sized enterprises
- Industrial consumers (auto, general engineering)
- Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities / emerging towns

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: Not applicable (distribution/marketplace model operates on immediate fulfillment); Steel volumes FY26: 1.016M tonnes; Q4: 2.89L tonnes.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: FY27 Revenue Growth: ~20%. FY27 Steel Volume: 1.2M tonnes (+~18-20%); FY28: 1.4M tonnes. FY27 Non-Steel Revenue: INR 750cr (+25%); FY28: INR 925cr. Margin Target: ~3.3-3.5% for FY27 (conservative), aspiring to 4% in 2-3 years (by FY29). Capex: INR 15-20cr for 7-10 new fulfillment centers in FY27.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Non-steel mix shift target (15-20% of revenue in 3-5 years vs <10% currently); Geographic penetration in Tier-2/3/4; New categories (UPVC roofing, electrical, paints); Store network expansion (7-10 new centers in FY27).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Sustained government capital expenditure, infrastructure expansion and urbanization continuing to support structural growth in building materials demand
- Government infrastructure programmes (PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan, National Infrastructure Pipeline, Smart Cities Mission, PM Awas Yojana, Jal Jeevan Mission) expected to generate sustained multi-year demand across steel, pipes, roofing and allied construction materials
- Steel demand growing at an estimated 8-10% year-on-year
- Retail building materials growth supported by rising home construction/renovation activity, growth in Tier-2/Tier-3 cities, increasing preference for branded/quality-assured products, expansion of contractor-led and project-based purchasing, and a shift from fragmented local procurement to integrated supply solutions
- Gradual, ongoing transition of the market from unorganised trade to organised retail and omni-channel distribution models, aided by growing digital adoption for product discovery and ordering
- India's economy expected to grow around 6.5-7% in FY27 per RBI/global analyst projections, supporting domestic demand, though geopolitical tensions (U.S.-Iran conflict), India's high fossil-fuel import dependence, rising petroleum prices and rupee depreciation are flagged as headwinds that could stoke inflation and dampen customer sentiment
- Company's high exposure to steel, a largely commoditised category, exposes it to periodic price volatility that can affect both demand patterns and margins

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: FY26 EBITDA margin 3.35% (up 47bps); Q4 margin 3.51%. Headwinds: Natural gas prices impacting tile supply chain; PVC resin volatility. Tailwinds: Operating leverage (expenses grew 7-8% vs revenue 30%); Product mix improvement; Safeguard duties stabilizing domestic steel prices.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Organic expansion of fulfillment network; Working capital optimization (25-day cycle); No M&A mentioned; Dividend policy not discussed in transcript.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: FY26 was dominated by the demerger of the omni-channel trading business from Shankara Building Products Limited into Shankara Buildpro Limited (NCLT Bengaluru Bench, appointed date April 1, 2024) and the Company's subsequent independent stock-exchange listing, creating a focused retail and distribution platform distinct from the parent's manufacturing/processing operations. Growth during the year came from continued geographic expansion of the omni-channel footprint into smaller cities and emerging towns and into Western and Central India (Maharashtra, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, Odisha), alongside build-out of the e-commerce channel (Buildpro Store plus Amazon and Flipkart), rather than from a named plant/capacity project — the business is an asset-light retail, distribution and e-commerce network (130 fulfilment centres including 95 stores) rather than a manufacturer.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on long-term structural story and volume targets; Conservative on near-term margin guidance (3.3-3.5%) despite strong operating leverage; Acknowledges Q1 softness but expects H2 recovery.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Extensive omni-channel distribution network of 130 fulfilment centres and 95 branded retail stores across South, West and Central India
- Long-standing partnerships with leading national brands across steel (JSW, SAIL, AM/NS India, APL Apollo) and non-steel categories (Jaquar, Kohler, Kajaria, Nippon Paint, Polycab, Havells)
- Established omni-channel presence combining physical stores/warehousing with own e-commerce platform (Buildpro Store) and marketplace listings (Amazon, Flipkart)
- Over five decades of industry experience and an established, diversified customer base across retail, contractor and institutional segments
- Deep market penetration strategy targeting smaller cities and emerging towns rather than only metros, supporting a resilient, geographically diversified revenue base

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body: Near-term demand slowdown in Q1 FY27 due to price hikes (tiles/steel); Morbi tile cluster supply disruptions; Raw material volatility (PVC, Gas); Competition from new-age startups and large corporates in metros; Execution risk on non-steel recovery.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body: Inventory gains/losses significantly impact quarterly PAT (Q4 had INR 15cr gain vs INR 8-9cr loss in prior quarters); Top 10 customers contribute only ~1% of revenue indicating extreme fragmentation; 50-50 split between retail and non-retail (OE/Dealer) in steel business.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demerger] The company is presented as post-demerger from Shankara Building Products Limited, with the RoCE of 35% in Q1FY27 explicitly attributed to that post-demerger structure; CIN L24311KA2023PLC179791 and the NSE/BSE listing (BUILDPRO / 544517) are those of the new entity.
- [Labour code] Footnote to the results slide: "FY26 PAT has an impact of ₹2.61 Crore on account of one-time provisioning due to labour code amendments."
- [Industry backdrop] The deck flags a "Tepid building materials environment continued across the industry" and describes non-steel revenue growth as having "resumed in Q1FY27, after a muted FY25 and FY26 impacted by macro headwinds".
- [Reporting basis] Notes state the figures are consolidated and rounded off; the 4Y CAGR figures are on an FY22-FY26 base.
